*The series aired on NBC throughout its run from 1966 to 1969. It aired on Thursdays for its first year.<ref>Gent, George. "Alex Segal to Produce 3 Danny Thomas TV Shows." ''[[The New York Times]]''. March 15, 1967: 9.5.</ref> The series was also done by Desilu Productions until 1967, when production switched to Paramount Television. 
*I conducted various copyright searches on the [http://onlinebooks.library.upenn.edu/cce/ UPenn] site to try determining if any copyrights had been registered.
*I searched the complete volumes for film and artwork for the years 1965 to 1969.  Desilu Productions registered only ''[[w:The Lucy Show]]'' and [[w:Yours, Mine and Ours (1968 film)]] in conjunction with Walden Films.  NBC registered only one still image-a color slide from ''Bonanza'' of Ben Cartwright on a horse.
*Nothing turned up when I searched ''Star Trek'' for the years 1965 through 1969 in either film or artwork.  
*There's no evidence of copyright for this time frame from either production company or from NBC.

ObjectName.value: 'Engineer of the Future'- Star Trek's 'Scotty,' James Doohan, Presents at NASA Goddard (James Doohan at GSFC 1992)

Categories.value: James Doohan|PD NASA|WebM videos|1992-03-02|NASA videos in 1992|Videos of 1992|Uploaded with video2commons|Files from NASA with known IDs|Betacam tape|NASA Library files uploaded by OptimusPrimeBot

ImageDescription.value: Famous for his portrayal of Chief Engineer Montgomery Scott -- "Scotty" -- on Star Trek, James Doohan visited NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, in March 1992. Doohan gave his presentation (entitled "Engineer of the Future") to a standing-room-only crowd in Goddard's Building 8 auditorium before answering questions from the audience. Doohan's appearance was not quite four months after "Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country" hit theaters, and little more than half-a-year before he reprised his role in an episode of "Star Trek: The Next Generation." Tom Huber, then Goddard's director of engineering, introduced Doohan, whose lecture was presented under the auspices of the Goddard Engineering Colloquium. This video recording of the presentation was digitized in June 2022 from a Betacam cassette copy found in the archives of the Office of Communications at Goddard.
